sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree before enrollment; UChicago degree qualifies in type, with no minimum GPA. Only PhD
admission for mathematics. International applicants eligible; most funding requires evidence of work
authorization at matriculation, so coordinate F-1 transfer/new Caltech documents with international office if
admitted. [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply to one academic option (Mathematics), prepare CV, essays, all-college transcripts and exactly three
referees; register writers early. Request hardship waiver within application if needed. No supervisor
pre-agreement stated. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior advisor agreement stated; specific research/prerequisite questions may be directed to option. Confirm
supervision capacity. Xinwen Zhu is not in current Caltech faculty roster (now Stanford); do not use historical
Caltech pages as current adviser evidence. [s3] [s13]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate central checklist, one academic option, automatic referee request upon registration, online receipt
checklist. Applicant uploads lock after submission; contact Graduate Office for major errors. [s3] [s4] [s7]
Cycle verification [Unresolved]
Standing December 10 math deadline; linked PDF named 2026-27 has 2024 revision and no explicit year in
table. Current stipend is 2026-27; essay details partly portal-only. [s1] [s5] [s9]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
English tests not required for admission; proficiency can be demonstrated through education. TOEFL, IELTS,
PTE, DET and other certified tests recognized if supplied, with no minimum score. Self-report permitted. [s3] [s8]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Exemption explicitly applies after two or more years of US study or an English-instruction degree. UChicago
education meets this route if either condition satisfied. Limited-English-background arrivals may be evaluated
separately. [s3]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required and will NOT be considered by Mathematics; central table labels General GRE not accepted. Do
not spend money sending these for math. [s1] [s8]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Exactly three: application accepts maximum three. Choose faculty/research supervisors familiar with ability;
relevant work supervisors may also evaluate. Prompts ask relationship, research capacity/motivation,
willingness to supervise, English capability and comparison with prior Caltech students. [s3] [s7]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No separate application for ordinary institutional financial support; no extra reference identified. Special
external/nationality-linked awards have independent rules. [s9] [s12]

What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Registering referee automatically sends upload-instruction email. Do not register until writer is ready. [s7]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Registration sends request before final application submission; not restricted to after submission. Public
checklist requires letters by deadline. [s4] [s7]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Online checklist shows received letters. Electronic preferred; FAQ permits paper/email if writer cannot upload,
with applicant identified. [s3] [s7]

Submitted supporting documents cannot be modified by applicant. Major errors go to Graduate Studies Office.
Referee ability to replace a submitted letter or reuse prior-cycle letters not established publicly. [s3]

Required upload. Include relevant teaching/work, research, academic honors/memberships,

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Institute PhD stipend US $50,000 gross/taxable for 12 months effective 1 September 2026; 2027-28 rate not
yet established. Full tuition/mandatory fees covered; health insurance only partly subsidized (about 80% per
admitted FAQ), remaining premium/dental/vision/parking not covered as mandatory fees. [s9] [s10] [s11]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math guarantees five years with satisfactory progress. Academic support October-June, summer
July-September typically RA or department fellowship. No summer support after fifth year; graduation expected
by June of year five. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Math support independent of domestic/international status; evidence of appropriate work authorization needed
for most funding appointments. [s1] [s2] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Full-time enrollment, satisfactory progress, securing thesis advisor and meeting program requirements.
Outside awards must be reported; outside employment requires prior written permission and generally limited
to eight hours weekly. [s9]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate application for ordinary institutional financial support; no extra reference identified. Special
external/nationality-linked awards have independent rules. [s9] [s12]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Institute/external fellowships, TA/RA; PMA math travel funds: one-time Bohnenblust $500 and up to $500
annually Groce, separate requests. Special fellowship eligibility varies. Central menu includes Taiwan/KAUTE/J.
Yang programs; citizenship-specific eligibility must be checked before treating as options. [s9] [s12] [s2]
Application fee [Standing rule]
US $100 institute graduate application fee, confirmed on official current division admissions page; exact
payment types not established on central public instructions. [s15]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Hardship form within application payment options, asks earned income/expenses and explanation. Reviewed
after application submitted; decision through admissions system. If denied, further hardship documentation or
payment allowed. No citizenship exclusion or separate request deadline published in FAQ. [s3]

admitted. [s2] [s3]

referees; register writers early. Request hardship waiver within application if needed. No supervisor
pre-agreement stated. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s7]

English requirement [Standing rule]

PTE, DET and other certified tests recognized if supplied, with no minimum score. Self-report permitted. [s3] [s8]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]

education meets this route if either condition satisfied. Limited-English-background arrivals may be evaluated
separately. [s3]

not spend money sending these for math. [s1] [s8]

One institution-issued transcript from every college/university attended; scan/university web transcript
acceptable, hand-typed course record not a substitute. Include grading legend/nonstandard-system
explanation. No updated in-progress term reports after submission. Official final attendance/degree records
required before enrollment if admitted. [s3] [s6] [s7]

willingness to supervise, English capability and comparison with prior Caltech students. [s3] [s7]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Institute PhD stipend US $50,000 gross/taxable for 12 months effective 1 September 2026; 2027-28 rate not
yet established. Full tuition/mandatory fees covered; health insurance only partly subsidized (about 80% per
admitted FAQ), remaining premium/dental/vision/parking not covered as mandatory fees. [s9] [s10] [s11]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math guarantees five years with satisfactory progress. Academic support October-June, summer
July-September typically RA or department fellowship. No summer support after fifth year; graduation expected
by June of year five. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Math support independent of domestic/international status; evidence of appropriate work authorization needed
for most funding appointments. [s1] [s2] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Full-time enrollment, satisfactory progress, securing thesis advisor and meeting program requirements.
Outside awards must be reported; outside employment requires prior written permission and generally limited
to eight hours weekly. [s9]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate application for ordinary institutional financial support; no extra reference identified. Special
external/nationality-linked awards have independent rules. [s9] [s12]

Institute/external fellowships, TA/RA; PMA math travel funds: one-time Bohnenblust $500 and up to $500
annually Groce, separate requests. Special fellowship eligibility varies. Central menu includes Taiwan/KAUTE/J.
Yang programs; citizenship-specific eligibility must be checked before treating as options. [s9] [s12] [s2]

US $100 institute graduate application fee, confirmed on official current division admissions page; exact
payment types not established on central public instructions. [s15]

Hardship form within application payment options, asks earned income/expenses and explanation. Reviewed
after application submitted; decision through admissions system. If denied, further hardship documentation or
payment allowed. No citizenship exclusion or separate request deadline published in FAQ. [s3]
